result.title: Tune for Retention, Not Just Gain: SFT Forgets Far Less than You Think
result.summary: Catastrophic forgetting, the drastic loss of previously acquired capabilities when learning new ones, is a central challenge in language model fine-tuning. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) is widely believed to be prone to such forgetting. Recent works have attributed this to the off-policy nature of SFT, arguing that on-policy learning is key to continual learning. In this paper, we challenge this premise. We show that while maximizing new-task performance can induce catastrophic forgetting, alternative hyperparameter choices (lower learning rate and batch size) can yield similar gains with little to no forgetting. With hyperparameters selected jointly for gain and retention, vanilla SFT retains prior capabilities far better than previously suggested and can be competitive with Self-Distillation Fine-Tuning (SDFT), an on-policy approach designed to mitigate forgetting. While SDFT can be more robust to hyperparameter choices, it also requires a retention-aware criterion to identify hyperparameter configurations that avoid catastrophic forgetting. Our results challenge the view that on-policy training is what enables learning with retention and raise broader questions about what drives catastrophic forgetting during fine-tuning.

AI.brief_summary: 论文反驳「SFT 因 off-policy 而必然导致灾难性遗忘」的前提，显示在联合考虑新任务收益与旧能力保持来选超参（更小学习率、batch size）时，vanilla SFT 的遗忘远小于此前认识，并可媲美 on-policy 的 SDFT。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文不涉及视觉或多模态推理，但其「为保持能力而选超参与保留判据」的做法，可能可供核查训练 VLM 推理或多阶段 latent 轨迹微调时如何避免削弱已有推理能力。
